sentences: I read the label on the paint can to check the base color and the drying time before I start.
I mix a small amount of blue tint into the white base on my palette to see the resulting shade.
I hold the paint chip against the wall to compare its color with the existing paint under the ceiling light.
I ask the clerk at the paint counter to scan the color code from my old can into the mixing machine.
I apply a second coat of paint after the first one dries to make the color look more even.
I check the finish sheen listed on the can to decide between matte, satin, or gloss for the trim.
I stir the paint can with a wooden stick before pouring to blend the pigments that settled at the bottom.
I paint a small square of the new color on the wall to test how it looks in the room.
I clean my brushes with solvent after using oil-based paint so the bristles do not harden.
I pour leftover paint into a smaller jar and label it with the room name and color code.
I use a roller to apply an even layer of paint on the ceiling without leaving visible streaks.
I tape off the window trim with blue painter's tape to keep the wall paint from bleeding onto it.
I notice the paint color on the wall changes when I turn on the incandescent lamp instead of the overhead light.
I read the tinting instructions on the bottle of universal colorant to add the correct number of drops.
I measure the square footage of the wall to calculate how many gallons of paint I need to buy.
I wipe the wet edge of the paint with a brush to avoid lap marks where the sections overlap.
I check the batch number printed on the can to ensure the color matches my previous purchase.
I apply a coat of white primer to cover the dark blue paint before I roll on the new color.
I scrape the dried paint from the rim of the can with a putty knife before I open it.
I pour the paint through a mesh strainer to remove any lumps or skin that formed in the can.
